title: Activation runway & feedback governance for first-10 lighthouse accounts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Create an operational runway that standardizes activation, onboarding, and feedback governance for the first 10 lighthouse customers so we can reliably validate product-market fit signals and surface regressions before wider beta. Scope includes: kickoff templates, onboarding checklist, measured success criteria, feedback loop cadence, rollout/rollback triggers, and release-notes coordination across SRE/Eng/Design/Support/CS/Marketing.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding checklist verified and used for 3 pilot activations
Launch notes and customer-facing FAQ published and linked from Console help
Feedback intake form, triage rubric, and priority SLAs agreed by Eng/SRE/CS
A dashboard tracking activation progress, errors, latency, and cost per session available to stakeholders
Canary rollback policy and fallback model selectors documented and tested in staging
stakeholders: Claire Nguyen - Head of Customer Success
Omar Haddad - Director of Reliability Engineering
launch_steps: Draft activation kickoff template and acceptance email (PM) - due 2026-03-05
Finalize onboarding checklist with Design and Support and run a dry-run internally (DES/Support) - due 2026-03-12
Wire up feedback intake form and triage board in JIRA/Confluence (PM/Eng) - due 2026-03-15
Publish customer-facing release notes + short FAQ in Console and Drive (PM/Marketing) - due 2026-03-18
Provision canary capacity and test rollback triggers with SRE (ENG) - due 2026-03-22
Activate first 3 lighthouse accounts in staged ramp, capture metrics and qualitative notes (CS/PM) - run 2026-03-25 to 2026-03-31
Weekly cross-functional sync during ramp with action item tracker and escalation path (PM lead)
success_metrics: Mean time to triage customer-reported regressions <= 4 hours
No P1 production incidents attributable to lighthouse activations
Net qualitative satisfaction > 8/10 from lighthouse interviews at week 2
Observed token cost per session within 10% of forecasted estimate
risks: Early lighthouse accounts exercise edge-case configs that require bespoke runtime fixes
Overload of CS/SRE during ramp if multiple accounts are activated concurrently
Ambiguous feedback leading to long debate cycles rather than actionable bugs
Release notes miss critical behavior changes for dedicated/private deployments
run_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Stagger activations by 48 hours to reduce SRE spike risk. Trade-off: slower feedback loop but safer operational profile.
Decision: Use a lightweight feedback form + scheduled 30-min interviews rather than open-ended issue ingestion to prioritize signal. Trade-off: less raw volume but higher signal-to-noise.

Decision: Ship minimum customer-facing release notes first and follow with deep technical appendix for dedicated/private customers. Trade-off: extra doc work but reduces early confusion for enterprise users.

notes: Prefer pragmatic, instrumented experiments over sweeping changes during lighthouse ramp. This work is intentionally small-batch to limit blast radius while providing clear telemetry. If ENG-4210 cannot be resolved before 3/22, we will postpone the first activation and run an extended internal beta with partners.
